summary: This experimental RFC describes boundary-node behavior for the Single Marking mode of Pre-Congestion Notification. It uses two marking states, not-marked and excess-traffic-marked, for measurement-based load control.

eli5.summary: Same idea as a traffic warning system, but with only two colors, so the guards have a simpler rule.

questions: what is pcn single marking mode
how does pcn sm mode differ from cl mode
what is the factor u in pcn sm
what clelimit does pcn sm recommend
subtitle: The two-state version of PCN edge behavior, trading some termination accuracy for a simpler core.

tldr.problem: Admitted voice and video flows need protection from overload in a Diffserv domain, ideally with the simplest possible marking support in interior nodes.
tldr.mechanism: Interior nodes use only two marking states, not-marked and excess-traffic-marked. Egress nodes report the rates, and the Decision Point admits or blocks flows by comparing the CLE to a limit and terminates flows using a contingency factor U times the not-marked rate.
tldr.outcome: It is an Experimental RFC. The text says SM is more likely than the CL mode of RFC 6661 to terminate too many flows when overload follows a failure.

today: RFC 6662 is an Experimental RFC and is not obsoleted or updated according to the metadata. The Controlled Load alternative is in RFC 6661.

sections.title: Introduction and the Experiment
sections.content:
Pre-Congestion Notification (PCN) protects the quality of service of inelastic flows in a Diffserv domain through admission control and, in abnormal circumstances, flow termination. Packets are marked when configured rates below the link rate are exceeded, so edge nodes get early notice of overload.

This document describes the experimental Single Marking (SM) edge behavior. It is a companion to RFC 6661, and the two share a great deal of text. The goals are to validate the specification, evaluate how well it preserves quality of service, and weigh PCN's cost savings against other methods.
sections.eli5: A warning system tells the gatekeepers that a road is nearly full. This version uses just one kind of warning.

sections.title: Assumed Core Behavior for SM
sections.content:
In SM mode interior nodes perform only excess-traffic-marking of PCN packets, following RFC 5670. For IP they use the excess-traffic-marked codepoint from RFC 6660. On each link the reference rate of the excess-traffic-meter is set equal to the PCN-admissible-rate.

So there are two marking states, not-marked and excess-traffic-marked, where CL mode has three. The roles are the same: the egress node measures and reports, the Decision Point decides, and the ingress node enforces.
sections.eli5: The road sensors use only one warning flag, so the sensors are simpler.

sections.title: Egress Measurements and Reporting
sections.content:
The egress node measures the rates of not-marked (NM-rate) and excess-traffic-marked (ETM-rate) traffic for each ingress-egress-aggregate over each measurement period T_meas, and reports them to the Decision Point. Optional report suppression works as in CL mode, but the congestion level estimate is CLE = ETM-rate / (NM-rate + ETM-rate), or zero if no traffic was seen.

With suppression on, a report is sent when the current or previous CLE exceeds the CLE-reporting-threshold or when T_maxsuppress has elapsed. The CLE-reporting-threshold MUST NOT exceed the CLE-limit at the Decision Point.
sections.eli5: Exit guards count flagged and unflagged cars and tell the boss the share that were flagged.

sections.title: Admission and Termination
sections.content:
Admission works as in CL mode: if the CLE is less than the configurable CLE-limit, the state is "admit", otherwise "block". For SM it is RECOMMENDED to set the CLE-limit fairly low, on the order of 5%.

Termination is triggered differently. When the admission state is "block", the Decision Point requests the PCN-sent-rate from the ingress node and waits for the next egress report. If that report still has a non-zero ETM-rate, the sustainable aggregate rate is estimated as SAR = U * NM-rate, where U is a configurable factor greater than one, the same for all aggregates. The amount to terminate is PCN-sent-rate - SAR.

U acts as a contingency buffer for flow peaks. A reasonable value is between 1.2 and 2, and larger values tend to cause more over-termination during peaks but raise average link utilization.
sections.eli5: When the gate is closed and cars are still flagged, the boss sends some away. The boss allows a bit more than the unflagged count, as a cushion.

sections.title: Missing Reports and Timers
sections.content:
As in CL mode, the Decision Point runs a failure timer that expires at T_fail (T_crit, or 3 * T_maxsuppress when suppression is on and the last CLE was at or below the threshold). On expiry it SHOULD notify management.

If a centralized Decision Point gets no reply about the PCN-sent-rate, it SHOULD repeat the request once. If the second request also fails, it SHOULD notify management. Unlike CL mode, SM has no fallback estimate for the amount to terminate. The recommended durations are the same as in CL mode, including T_meas of 100 to 500 ms.
sections.eli5: If a guard goes quiet, the boss raises an alarm. If the entry guard does not answer twice, the boss tells the managers.

sections.title: Deployment, Applicability and Security
sections.content:
The behavior suits inelastic traffic such as voice and video. The text says performance results indicate that SM is more likely to terminate too many flows than CL after events such as rerouting. Deployment follows the same steps as CL mode, plus choosing U. Packets are classified by ingress-egress-aggregate, which reliably needs tunnels, and event logging via syslog and counters are specified.

The security considerations are those of RFC 5559, plus one new one: with a centralized Decision Point, the interface on the ingress node must be protected from denial-of-service attacks.
sections.eli5: Setup is like the three-flag version, plus choosing the cushion size. The boss's phone line needs protection too.
